unit_description: This unit connects area to multiplication. Students tile rectangles with unit squares, connect rows and columns to multiplication, find the area of rectangles and squares, and solve area word problems.
unit_goals: Connect rows and columns to multiplication.
Find the area of rectangles and squares.
Understand the area formula for rectangles.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students connect tiling rectangles to multiplication and use multiplication to find the area of rectangles and squares.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by matching multiplication facts to arrays.
lessons.concept: A rectangle can be covered with unit squares in rows and columns. The number of rows times the number of columns tells how many unit squares fit.
lessons.practice: Tile rectangles with unit squares and write the multiplication equation.
lessons.objective: Tile rectangles with unit squares and connect to multiplication.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 4 squares long and 3 squares wide. How many squares cover it?
How many rows are in a 5 by 2 rectangle?
questions.hint: The first number is the number of rows.

questions.prompt: A square has 6 rows and 6 columns. How many unit squares?

learn.title: Tile Rectangles with Unit Squares
teaching_points: Cover the rectangle with unit squares.
Multiply rows times columns to find the total.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Tile a 3 by 7 rectangle. What is the area?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Tile each rectangle and write the multiplication equation for the area.

flashcards.title: Tiling Rectangles
flashcards.instructions: Review tiling rectangles with unit squares.

bigIdea.title: Tile Rectangles with Unit Squares
bigIdea.subtitle: Rows and columns cover the rectangle
bigIdea.intro: When you tile a rectangle with unit squares, the squares line up in rows and columns. The total number of squares is the area.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is tiling a rectangle like building an array?

ruleCards.description: Count how many rows of unit squares fit.
Count how many squares fit in each row.

lessons.lesson_title: Connect Rows and Columns to Multiplication
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by writing multiplication equations for rows and columns.
lessons.concept: The area of a rectangle is the number of rows times the number of columns. This is the same as length times width. Area = rows × columns.
lessons.practice: Use multiplication to find the area of rectangles from rows and columns.
lessons.objective: Connect rows and columns to multiplication to find area.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with rows and columns.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has 4 rows and 9 columns. What is the area?
What multiplication equation gives the area of a 7 by 5 rectangle?

learn.title: Connect Rows and Columns to Multiplication
teaching_points: The number of rows is one factor.
The number of columns is the other factor.

example.prompt: Find the area of a rectangle with 6 rows and 8 columns.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle has 5 rows and 8 columns. What is the area?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Multiply rows by columns to find the area of each rectangle.

bigIdea.title: Connect Rows and Columns to Multiplication
bigIdea.subtitle: Area is rows times columns
bigIdea.intro: A rectangle's area can be found by multiplying the number of rows by the number of columns. This is the same as length times width.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does rows × columns give the area?

ruleCards.description: The number of rows is one factor in the area.
The number of columns is the other factor.

lessons.lesson_title: Find the Area of Rectangles and Squares
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by multiplying side lengths to find areas.
lessons.concept: The area of a rectangle is length times width. A square has equal length and width, so area is side × side.
lessons.practice: Find the area of rectangles and squares using multiplication.
lessons.objective: Find the area of rectangles and squares using length and width.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with length and width.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 7 units long and 4 units wide. What is the area?
A square has sides of 5 units. What is the area?

learn.title: Find the Area of Rectangles and Squares
teaching_points: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
Area of a square = side × side.
Label the answer in square units.

example.prompt: Find the area of a rectangle with length 8 and width 6.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Find the area of a square with side length 9.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find the area of each rectangle or square.

flashcards.title: Area of Rectangles and Squares
flashcards.instructions: Review length, width, side, and area.

bigIdea.title: Find the Area of Rectangles and Squares
bigIdea.subtitle: Length × width = area
bigIdea.intro: For any rectangle, you can multiply length times width to find the area. For a square, length and width are the same, so side times side gives the area.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is a square a special kind of rectangle?

ruleCards.description: A square has all sides equal.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by identifying length and width in word problems.
lessons.concept: Area word problems give the length and width or ask for one of them. Write a multiplication or division equation to solve. Area = length × width, so length = area ÷ width.
lessons.practice: Solve word problems about the area of rectangles and squares.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with area word problems.

questions.prompt: A rug is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide. What is the area?
A garden has an area of 36 square meters and a width of 4 meters. What is the length?
A poster is 5 inches by 9 inches. What is the area?

learn.title: Solve Area Word Problems
teaching_points: Find the length and width in the problem.
Divide if you know the area and one side.

example.prompt: A desk is 8 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is the area?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A room is 10 feet long and 8 feet wide. What is the area?

bigIdea.title: Solve Area Word Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: Use length × width
bigIdea.intro: Area word problems are about real spaces. Find the length and width, multiply them, and use the right square unit label.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you do if a word problem gives the area and one side?

ruleCards.description: Multiply the two side lengths to find area.
Divide the area by the known side to find the missing side.

lessons.lesson_title: Unit Evaluation: Multiplying to Find Area
lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of tiling rectangles, rows and columns, area of rectangles and squares, and area word problems.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: tiling rectangles with unit squares, connecting rows and columns to multiplication, finding the area of rectangles and squares, and solving area word problems.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about multiplying to find area.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 8 by 7. What is the area?
A square has side length 6. What is the area?
A rug is 9 feet by 5 feet. What is the area?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: tiling + rows/columns + rectangles/squares + word problems = multiplying to find area

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle has 6 rows and 7 columns. What is the area?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 21 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 21 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Multiplying to Find Area
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: tiling rectangles with unit squares, connecting rows and columns to multiplication, finding the area of rectangles and squares, and solving area word problems.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about multiplying to find area?

ruleCards.description: Multiply the side lengths to find the area of a rectangle.
A square has equal length and width.
